q: What is one fidel character?
o: The name of an English letter
Only a vowel, with no consonant
why: One fidel character writes a consonant and a vowel together.

q: What is true of the sixth order?
o: It is always the vowel of see
It always marks a long consonant
It may be a vowel or no vowel, and the spelling does not say which
It is always the vowel of father
why: The sixth order may be a short vowel or no vowel, and you learn which by listening.

q: Why can ገና be two different words?
o: Amharic writes a long consonant twice
A long consonant and a short one are written the same way
The sixth order is always silent
why: The fidel writes a long consonant once, so one spelling can hold two meanings.

q: In Addis Ababa, ሀ and ሐ are…
o: One h sound, spelled with two letters
why: ሀ and ሐ are one h in Addis Ababa. The spelling still keeps them apart.

q: What is ቀ?
o: An ejective, not a plain k
why: ቀ is an ejective. The plain k letter has not been taught yet, and it is not this one.

q: Why do ሀ and ሃ sound alike?
o: Every first order uses the father vowel
ሀ is an exception: its first order uses the father vowel, like its fourth order
why: For ሀ and ሐ, the first order and the fourth order share the father vowel.

q: In Addis Ababa, how many h sounds do ሀ, ሐ, ኀ and ኸ make?
why: Those four letters are one h in Addis Ababa. Words still keep their own spelling.

q: What do አ and ዐ do?
o: They write a vowel with no consonant, and in Addis Ababa they share that job
why: አ and ዐ are vowel carriers. They do the same job in Addis Ababa.

q: ከ and ቀ are…
o: A plain k and an ejective, two consonants
why: ከ is a plain k. ቀ is an ejective. Do not trade them.

q: ጠ and ተ are…
o: An ejective and a plain t, two consonants
A long t and a short t
why: ጠ is an ejective. ተ is a plain t. The length of a consonant is a different issue, and it is not written.

q: ፀ and ጸ are…
o: A plain s and an ejective
why: ፀ and ጸ are the same ejective ts. ሰ is the plain s.

q: What does አቶ ከበደ use አቶ for?
o: A title before a man's name
why: አቶ sits before a man's name. It is a title, not a greeting.

q: In Addis Ababa, ጸ and ፀ are…
o: A plain s and an ejective
why: ጸ and ፀ are the same ejective ts. The plain s letters are ሰ and ሠ.

q: ኳ is the -wa form on…
why: ኳ is plain k plus w. ቧ is b, and ጓ is g.

q: You see ገና with no audio and no context. What can you know?
o: It is one of those two, and the letters do not say which
The n is written twice if it is long
why: ገና is still or Christmas. The long consonant is not written.

q: You walk into a shop and greet a stranger. You do not know the hour. What fits?
why: ጤና ይስጥልኝ is the formal hello for any person and any time of day.

q: Good morning to a woman is…
why: The woman form in the morning is አደርሽ. ዋልሽ is afternoon.

q: አመሰግናለሁ is said to…
o: anyone, because the ending means I
why: አመሰግናለሁ means I thank, so the ending does not change for the listener.

q: Abebech gives her name. Which sentence is right?
why: The subject is ስም, so the verb ending is ነው, even though Abebech is a woman.

q: You ask a woman her name. Which is right?
why: The woman form is ስምሽ, and the verb ending stays ነው.

q: You ask an older stranger their name. Which is right?
why: The polite form is ስምዎ, and the verb ending is ነው.

q: She is fine. Which is the form to learn?
why: እሷ is feminine, so the verb ending is ናት. ነው is the he form.

q: We are fine. Which is right?
why: The verb ending ነን agrees with the subject እኛ.

q: You are speaking to one older stranger. You are fine, addressed to them, is…
why: The polite form for the person you are talking to is ነዎት.

q: How does Amharic say the for a house?
o: With a small word before ቤት
why: The masculine definite ending is on the noun: ቤቱ.

q: The girl is…
why: ልጇ is the feminine form. ልጁ is the boy.

q: Houses, more than one, is…
why: The plural ending is -ኦች: ቤቶች. An English s is not the plural.

q: How do you say this for a book?
why: A book is masculine, so this is ይህ.

q: Which sentence is 'This is Tigist'?
why: Tigist is a woman, so use ይህች and the verb ending ናት.

q: 'That is a pen' =
why: A pen farther away takes ያ, and the verb ending is ነው.

q: 'Where is the house?' =
why: የት asks where. There is no helper like do.

q: 'Who are you?' to a woman =
why: አንቺ takes the woman form ነሽ.

q: 'How are you?' to a stranger =
why: እርስዎ takes the polite form ነዎት.

q: Five =
why: Five is አምስት. ስድስት is six.

q: 'They are two houses' =
why: More than one takes the verb ending ናቸው. This line keeps ቤት singular.

q: Twenty =
why: Twenty is its own word, ሃያ. ሀያ is the same word.

q: 'Your house,' to a woman =
why: The woman form is ቤትሽ. ቤቷ is her house.

q: 'It is my house' =
why: The verb ending ነው agrees with the house, not with I.

q: 'Your house,' to an older stranger =
why: The polite form is ቤትዎ.

q: 'I have a pen' =
why: The thing comes first. The verb ending አለኝ is I.

q: 'You do not have a book,' to a woman =
why: The woman form of the negative is የለሽም.

q: Said with a long l, አለ means
why: The long l means there is. The short l, same letters, means he said.

q: 'I am from America' =
why: ከ joins the place, and I takes ነኝ, not the man form ነህ.

q: 'This book is for you,' to a woman =
why: ለ joins the person. The book is masculine, so the verb ending is ነው.

q: 'You are in Addis Ababa,' polite =
why: በ is in, joined to the place, and እርስዎ takes the polite form ነዎት.

q: 'I drank the coffee' =
why: The definite object takes ን, and the verb ending ጠጣሁ is I.

q: 'You went,' to a woman =
why: The woman form is ሄድሽ. ሄደች is she went.

q: 'She went home' =
why: The feminine verb ending is ሄደች, and it comes last.

q: 'I will go home' =
why: እሄዳለሁ is I go and I will go. ሄድኩ is the past.

q: 'You drink coffee,' to a woman =
why: The woman form is ትጠጫለሽ. ትጠጣለሽ leaves the consonant unpalatalized.

q: 'He goes to Gondar' =
why: The masculine verb ending is ይሄዳል, after the place.

q: 'I did not go' =
why: The past negative wraps the past form: አልሄድኩም. አልሄድም is the present.

q: 'You did not go home,' to a woman =
why: The woman form is አልሄድሽም, and the verb comes last.

q: 'I do not go' =
why: The present negative is the short form አልሄድም.

q: Where does እፈልጋለሁ go in "I want coffee"?
o: In the middle, as in English
why: The thing comes first and the verb comes last: ቡና እፈልጋለሁ.

q: "I want to go" uses which word before want?
why: Want takes the infinitive, the to-form መሄድ, not a second finished verb.

q: Which form is said to a woman?
why: The woman form is ትፈልጊያለሽ. ትፈልጋለህ is the man form.

q: How do you say "Come!" to a woman?
why: The woman form of come is ነይ. ና is the man form.

q: How do you say "please" to a stranger?
why: A stranger is እርስዎ, so please is እባክዎ.

q: ተቀመጡ is said to…
why: ተቀመጡ is the plural. The polite form is ይቀመጡ.

q: Abebech asks a stranger the time. She starts with…
why: The manual says ይቅርታ before you ask a stranger the time.

q: ጠዋት አስራ ሁለት ሰዓት is…
why: The manual's pair: Ethiopian 12 in the morning is 6 a.m.

q: Which Wednesday does this course write?
why: The manual writes ሮብ. ረቡዕ is another spelling you may see, not a mistake.

q: How do you ask the price?
why: The price you both mean is ዋጋው, and one price takes ነው.

q: The manual's coffee figure is for practice. It is…
why: The book says coffee is four birr. That is not a claim about today's menu.

q: ሂሳብ ስንት ነው asks…
why: ሂሳብ is the bill. ስንት ነው asks how much.

q: "I like coffee" is…
why: The thing comes first. እፈልጋለሁ means I want, not I like.

q: Which word is the feminine form of ውብ?
why: The manual marks ውቢት as the feminine word. ቆንጆ does not change in that way.

q: What does this lesson teach you to say after a compliment?
o: A special reply from the manual
ምንም አይደለም as the set reply
Nothing. A checked reply is not in the sources
why: A reply to a compliment was not in the sources, so it is not taught here.

q: How do you say "your father" to a woman?
why: The woman form is አባትሽ. አባትህ is the man form.

q: "I have no brother" is…
why: የለኝም is the negative of አለኝ. ወንድም is brother.

q: My sister is in Addis Ababa. The last word is…
why: እህቴ is feminine, so the verb ending is ናት.

q: You want injera. What comes first?
why: The food comes first, then want.

q: Please, to a woman server you know, is…
why: እባክሽ is please to a woman. እባክህ is the man form.

q: ፍርፍር on this menu is…
why: The manual treats እንጀራ as the base of ፍርፍር.

q: "Where is the hotel?" ends with…
why: The hotel is the subject, so the verb ending is ነው.

q: "Go left" to a woman starts with…
why: The place comes first: ወደ ግራ ሂጂ.

q: "Where are you?" to እርስዎ is…
why: The polite form is ነዎት.
